O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. The short question that falls for consideration is wheth  the appellant has been paid compensation for the acquired land at  par with similarly placed expropriated land o  acquisition.

3. It appears from the record that the State of U.P. acquir  the appellants land bearing Khasra No.613, 
 hectares, situated at village Maleshemau, Tehsil   Lucknow, U.P., along with lands of various other villages.

It was rejected on the ground of delay.
4. The appellant laid challenge to that order before the Hi  2 Court in W.P. No.11892/2019, which was disposed of on 23.07.2019 in the following terms:

The stand of the State is that award was passed on  18.02.2018 while the Government Order has been issued  on 15.02.2017 and therefore the same will not be  applicable in the case of the petitioner and prays  for dismissal of the writ petition.

As per para-23 of  the counter-affidavit wherein the State has admitted  that compensation in terms of the award dated  03.02.2015 has been paid in compliance of the orders  dated 08.05.2017 and 25.07.2018 passed by this Court  in Writ Petition No.29128 (LA) of 2016 and Writ  Petition No.14595 (LA) of 2017 respectively.
It is  also pointed out by the learned Standing Counsel that

after passing of award, the petitioner filed a writ  petition for grant of similar benefit but the  aforesaid writ petition was disposed of by directing  the petitioner to challenge the ward by invoking Section 64 of Right to Fair Compensation and  Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and  Re-settlement Act, 2013.

sentences.text: The said application of the  petitioner was dismissed on the ground that the same  has been filed after the delay of two years, three  months and twelve days and therefore the petitioner  is not entitled for any benefit in terms of the order  passed on 08.05.2017 and 25.07.2018 and prays for  rejection of that application.

On due consideration of the aforesaid facts and  circumstances, so also the admission made by the  State in para-23 of the counter-affidavit, we dispose Manoj Kumar Yadav vs The State Of Uttar Pradesh on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59219051/
2  of the writ petition in terms of the order dated  08.05.2017 and 25.07.2018 by directing the  respondents to proceed in the matter keeping in view  the Government Order dated 15.02.2017 and pass a  speaking and reasoned order within a period of six  weeks from the date of presentation of the certified  copy of this order before the competent authority.

sentences.text: With the aforesaid, the writ petition is  disposed of.

5. It further appears that the appellant had also filed a fresh Writ Petition before the High Court claiming compensation at the rate as was awarded for semi-urban lands vide an Award dated 14.08.2015.
Such a claim is discernible from a representation dated 06.05.2016 made by the appellant for enhancement of compensation.

3 This Writ Petition i.e., Writ Petition No.23881/2018 (LA) was disposed of by the High Court on 21.08.2018, followed by the Writ Petition No. 11892/2019 (LA) in which the grounds taken in the previous Writ Petition were reiterated.
This Writ Petition too was disposed of by the High Court on 23.07.2019 vide an order, the operative part of which has already been reproduced above.

6. It may be mentioned that the first Writ Petition, i.e.,
W.P.No.26360/2019, has been dismissed by the High Court vide the impugned order dated 22.06.2021.
7.

As the facts would speak for themselves, the appellant has been misdirected in initiating Writ Petitions one after the other before the High Court without specifically raising the issue of parity so as to seek the same compensation as was granted to the other interested persons of the same acquisition process.

8. The orders passed by the High Court summarily in these Writ Petitions also do not enlighten the claim(s) raised by the Manoj Kumar Yadav vs The State Of Uttar Pradesh on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59219051/
3 appellant.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Ordinarily, in a case where there is a delay in filing the appeal or reference etc., the expropriated land owners can be granted parity in compensation without granting them the benefit of interest for the delayed period.
Such an equitable recourse has been followed by this Court in a catena of decisions.

9. It goes without saying that if the other land owners have been granted higher compensation by the Collector, Reference Court or the High Court, there is no rhyme or reason to deny the appellant the benefit of such enhancement, merely on account of the delay of more than two years in raising the reference.

As observed above,
the Court could have instead denied him interest for the delayed  4 period only.
10. The multiple writ petitions filed by the appellant and the orders passed pursuant thereto have compounded the confusion.
There is no specific material to show that the other claimants of the same acquisition process have been granted compensation at a higher rate.
The plea raised to this effect by the appellant before the High Court has not been unfortunately controverted or rejected.

We are,
thus, not sure as to whether the appellant has been able to make out a case of parity, and if so, what is the legal basis to deny such parity to him except that he might not be entitled to interest for the delayed period.

11. In such circumstances, we deem it appropriate to remit the case to the High Court with a request to call for the records and determine (i) what is the rate of compensation that has been granted to the land owners affected by the same acquisition in which the Manoj Kumar Yadav vs The State Of Uttar Pradesh on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59219051/
4 land of the appellant was also acquired vide Notification dated 16.08.2011?

entities.text: Manoj Kumar Yadav vs The State Of Uttar Pradesh on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (ii) If other land owners have been granted higher rate of compensation, why has the appellant been denied such parity except grant of interest for the delayed period?

12. Consequently, we set aside the two orders passed by the High Court i.e. order dated 23.07.2019, passed in W.P.No.11892/2019,
and the impugned order dated 22.06.2021 passed in Writ Petition No.26360/2019.

The High Court is requested to take up both the Writ Petitions together and determine the question formulated above after obtaining necessary information through an additional affidavit to be filed by the State of U.P. and its authorities.

13. The High Court is requested to decide the matter afresh  5 and in accordance with law as early as possible, and preferably within six months.
14.
It is clarified that we have not expressed any opinion on the merits of the case.
15. The parties are directed to appear before the High Court on 24.07.2024.
16. The appeal stands disposed of in the above terms.
17. As a result, the pending interlocutory applications also stand disposed of.
